column1: Article 113's own text
# T210 - gap 108 WAS NOT A CONTRADICTION. p168 recorded "one source puts 50(2) watermarking at
# 2 December 2026 and another says Article 50 has applied since 2 August 2026" as two readings 15 months
# apart. They are both correct and they do not conflict: 2 August 2026 is the APPLICATION DATE of the
# duty; 2 December 2026 is a TRANSITIONAL CARVE-OUT that applies only to the machine-readable marking
# limb and only to systems already on the market before the application date. The gap was a SCOPE
# confusion between a duty's start and a grandfathering window, and this KB manufactured it by placing
# two true statements side by side without their scopes.
# WHAT STAYS OPEN, narrower (gap 110): the legal basis is still unread. Article 113 is the provision
# that sets application dates and NOT ONE of the 9 sources quotes it. So the 2 August 2026 date rests
# on nine secondary sources agreeing, which is not the same as reading the article. Tier
# search-summary, not promotable under T160.
# ALTERNATIVE FINDING, as pre-registered: the refusal is recorded and it is now CHARACTERISED. eur-lex
# fails as ENOTFOUND on WebFetch and 000 on curl - no DNS and no route, NOT a policy denial. Combined
# with T211 (gnu.org moved 403 -> 000 between containers), the 403-vs-000 distinction p168 drew cannot
# be read as "the gateway refuses this host on policy". For a FUTURE pass: this question needs a
# container whose egress allows eur-lex.europa.eu, and it needs ONE fetch of Article 113. Nothing
# else about it is worth re-litigating.
